html:
SMTO-DB-0007 — The database sign-in details weren't in a form SMTO accepts

GUID: fea764aa-f904-48e7-b4cf-70c74f2a40d4
Slug: database-auth-fields-invalid
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was given database sign-in details that were incomplete or in the wrong form. It only accepts a user name and a password, written as plain text. Nothing was sent to your database.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. When SMTO asks for database sign-in details, reply with just the user name and the password, and nothing else. SMTO only accepts these two values and refuses anything extra.
  2. To avoid typing them each time, open Parameter Store, select the database entry, select Reveal & edit value on the Value tab, fill in user and password, and select Save. Details saved there are used automatically and kept private.
  3. Make sure the password isn't placed inside the host name, the database address or the entry's description. Sign-in details in those places could be shown to others and are not read as a password.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects to the database and returns results without asking for sign-in details again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't include the password in that message or anywhere in the conversation beyond SMTO's own sign-in question.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Database authentication input was rejected: auth_values contained keys other than user/password or non-string values, or a discovery request had an empty user or password.

What this means

  • auth_values contains unsupported keys or non-string values, or discovery is missing a required nonempty user/password value. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • auth_values contains unsupported keys or non-string values, or discovery is missing a required nonempty user/password value.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish auth_values schema rejection from a missing discovery user or password; neither proves the server rejected credentials.

How to fix it

  • auth_values accepts only the keys user and password, each a string; any other key or a non-string value raises before execution. Discovery requests need a nonempty user and password. Supply them through the normal ask_user flow (the agent asks for all missing values together and passes them as transient auth_values, which are not saved), or save them in the Parameter Store entry's user/password fields; never in the host, URL, description or a public diagnostic.
  • Correct user/password field types and supply any required missing values through the supported private credential flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Only supported string login fields are supplied through the private credential flow.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
